Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

quite adverb

fairly, to some degree

also fairly, pretty, rather, somewhat, reasonably, a bit

classical

Cic. Off. 3.58: nec īnfacētus et satis litterātus
Cic. Off. 2.89: satis bene pāscere

satis

adverb, with adjectives and adverbs: satis bene, satis bonus

quite, fairly, well enough

Like English “enough”, satis can lower a quality: “tolerably, pretty, fairly” (Lewis & Short); satis bene, quite well.

Other words

  • aliquantum — somewhat, rather; quite a bit

    adverb; with a genitive, quite a lot of · also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 106: Aliquantum, soror, “Somewhat, sister”; Cic. Div. 2.3: mihi quidem ipsī sānē aliquantum medētur (Lewis & Short)

    Latin also says “rather” with the comparative (longior, rather long) or with sub-: subtristis, rather glum (Ter. And. 447); subdifficilis, rather hard (Cic. Amic. 67).

Examples

  • nec īnfacētus et satis litterātus

    not without wit, and quite well readCic. Off. 3.58

  • respondit: ‘bene pāscere’; quid secundum: ‘satis bene pāscere’

    he answered, “good grazing”; and second best? “quite good grazing”Cato in Cic. Off. 2.89

  • Subtristis vīsus est esse aliquantulum mihi.

    He seemed to me a little on the glum side.Ter. And. 447

See also quite, a little.
